turns.content: Hey, I've been dealing with a lot of work stress lately. My manager keeps piling on projects and I'm struggling to keep up.

I'm sorry to hear you're feeling overwhelmed at work. That's a really common experience, especially when workloads aren't distributed fairly. Can you tell me more about what's happening? Are there specific projects causing the most pressure?
It's mainly this quarterly report that's due next week. I've been working late every night and my manager just added two more client presentations to my plate.

That sounds like a lot to handle all at once. Working late consistently can really take a toll. Have you been able to communicate with your manager about your current capacity? Sometimes supervisors don't realize how much is already on someone's plate.
I tried mentioning it but she just said everyone's busy right now. I don't want to seem like I can't handle things, you know?

I understand that concern - many people worry about how they'll be perceived if they push back on workload. But advocating for reasonable expectations isn't the same as being incapable. Would it help to prioritize tasks together? Sometimes breaking things down makes it feel more manageable.
Maybe. I just feel like I'm falling behind no matter how hard I work. My coworkers seem to handle everything fine.

It's easy to compare ourselves to others, but we rarely see the full picture of what someone else is dealing with - or struggling with privately. You're clearly putting in significant effort. Are you getting enough rest between these long work days?
Not really. I've been sleeping maybe 4-5 hours a night. I keep waking up thinking about deadlines.

Sleep deprivation can really compound stress and make everything feel harder than it needs to be. Racing thoughts at night are a common sign of anxiety. Have you tried any wind-down routines, or is your mind just too active when you try to rest?
I've tried but my brain won't shut off. I used to go to the gym to decompress but I haven't had time for that in weeks.

Losing those healthy outlets can create a difficult cycle - you need stress relief the most when you have the least time for it. Even short walks or 10-minute stretching sessions can help. Is there anyone at home or in your life who's been supportive during this busy period?
My girlfriend has been patient but I can tell she's getting frustrated. We barely see each other anymore and when we do I'm just exhausted.

Relationship strain during high-stress work periods is really common, and it's good that she's been patient. It might help to have an honest conversation with her about what you're going through - letting her know this isn't the norm you want either. Does she understand how much pressure you're under?
I think so but lately she's been going out with her friends more. I don't blame her, I'm not exactly fun to be around right now.

It's understandable that she needs social time too, and it's actually healthy that she has that outlet. Try not to be too hard on yourself - being exhausted doesn't make you a bad partner. This is a temporary situation. Have you two been able to plan anything to look forward to once this crunch period passes?
We talked about a weekend trip but honestly I can't even imagine having free time right now. Everything just feels like it's piling up.

When we're in the thick of stress, it can be hard to see past it. But having something to look forward to, even if it feels distant, can be motivating. The crunch will eventually end. In the meantime, are you eating okay? Taking care of basics?
Mostly coffee and whatever's fast. I know it's not great. I just don't have the energy to cook or really do anything besides work.

That's a common pattern when overwhelmed, but nutrition does affect mood and energy levels. Even small improvements - keeping some easy healthy snacks around - could help. It sounds like work has taken over most aspects of your life right now. How long has this intense period been going on?
About two months now. They keep saying it'll slow down but it never does. I'm starting to wonder if this is just how it's going to be.

Two months is a long time to sustain that pace. It's reasonable to feel worn down. If the 'temporary' crunch keeps extending indefinitely, that might be worth addressing more directly with leadership - or considering whether this role is sustainable long-term. What made you take this job originally?
I thought it would be a good career move. Now I'm not sure it was worth it. I feel like I'm just going through the motions every day.

Feeling like you're on autopilot is a sign of burnout. The initial excitement or purpose you had has been drained by unsustainable demands. It's worth reflecting on what you actually want - not just in your career, but in your daily life. What would feel meaningful to you right now?
I honestly don't know anymore. Things I used to enjoy just feel like chores now. Even the weekend doesn't excite me.

Losing interest in things that used to bring joy is something to pay attention to. It can happen with prolonged stress and exhaustion. Have you noticed this affecting your mood overall, beyond just feeling tired?
Yeah, I guess I've been feeling pretty low. Like nothing really matters that much. I just do what I have to do to get through each day.

I hear you, and I want you to know that what you're describing - the exhaustion, loss of interest, feeling like things don't matter - these are signs that you're running on empty. This goes beyond normal work stress. Have you considered talking to someone, like a therapist or counselor, about how you've been feeling?
I've thought about it but scheduling another appointment feels like one more thing on the list. Plus I'm not even sure what I'd say. I'm just tired.

That tiredness you're describing sounds deep - not just physical but emotional too. You don't need to have the right words to talk to a professional; they're trained to help you work through feelings like this. Many offer virtual appointments that might be easier to fit in. How long have you been feeling this low?
A few weeks maybe? It kind of crept up. I stopped reaching out to friends because I don't have the energy to pretend everything's fine.

Withdrawing from friends is understandable when you're depleted, but isolation can make those low feelings intensify. You don't have to pretend with real friends - you could let them know you're going through a hard time. Is there anyone you feel you could be honest with?
Not really. Everyone has their own problems. I don't want to burden anyone with mine.

Feeling like a burden is a painful thought, but it's often not how the people who care about us actually see it. Your struggles are valid and worth sharing. I'm a bit concerned about how isolated you're feeling. Can you tell me more about what's going through your mind when you're alone?
Just a lot of negative thoughts I guess. Like wondering what the point of all this effort is. I work and work and nothing gets better.

Those thoughts about there being no point - that's something I want to take seriously. When you say nothing gets better, do you mean at work specifically, or does it feel broader than that, like life in general?
I don't know. Both I guess. I just feel stuck in this cycle that's never going to change. Sometimes I think everyone would be fine without me around.

I'm really glad you shared that with me, and I want to be direct with you - thoughts like 'everyone would be fine without me' are a sign that you need support right now. You matter, and what you're going through is serious but treatable. These feelings can get better with help. Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or not wanting to be here?
Not like a plan or anything. Just sometimes when I'm lying awake at night I think about how much easier it would be to just... not exist. To not feel this tired anymore.

Thank you for trusting me with that. What you're describing - those thoughts of not existing, of escaping the exhaustion - these are signs you need real human support right now, not just our conversation. I care about your safety. Please reach out to a crisis line like 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline) where you can talk to someone trained to help. You can call or text anytime. Will you do that today?
